    Session · 7:00 PM ET · weekdays

    The Evening Court

    After the close the day's leads are scored against the tape, the Pyramid re-forms, every seat files on base, off base and a lesson, the dossiers refresh and the model population trains — with its numbers in the court's own appendix.

    What the court is#

    The Evening Court is the day's accountability session. At 7:00 PM ET (editable under Settings) boardroom.retrospective.run_evening_review() takes the day's completed run, scores every lead against the closing tape, re-forms the Pyramid on the realized returns, and has every seat — the thirteen graders, the Skeptic and the Executive, fifteen entries — write a personal self-review: where they were on base, where they were off base, and the one durable lesson they take. The entries go to each member's journal, the journals regenerate the member dossiers, and then — last, on purpose — the model population runs its nightly generation. You can convene the court by hand with Run evening review on the Boardroom page or from the empty Evening view. A run already journaled is skipped unless forced; the button forces a fresh set of entries.

    The court is preceded by the 16:45 outcomes job: realized 1-day and 5-day returns are recorded for every lead whose trading-day window has closed (short leads sign-flipped), the Paper League is marked to market, and the outcome model retrains. The court records outcomes again itself — cheap and idempotent — before it scores.

    How the court runs#

    Scoring against the close#

    For each lead the court fetches today's close from a two-day daily history and computes the day return from the briefing price, signed by direction — a short that fell earns a positive number, and the view's footnote says it: "positive means the call was right". Option leads carry their contract label, the morning's last premium and a best-effort refetch of the contract's current last, open interest and volume; the persisted row also carries a flat contract_last (the evening refetch when it worked, else the morning's). A close that cannot be fetched leaves the return unavailable rather than zero. The scored rows plus the market-at-the-close context go to evening_reviews, one row per run, replaced on a re-run — that is what the Evening view and the PDF replay.

    On base, off base, lesson#

    Each grading seat and the Skeptic is shown only its own morning grades, stances and comments beside the realized day returns — no other member's grades and no final grades, because the ranking is the Executive's to answer for. The Executive is shown its own final ranking with the returns, its morning memo, the full Pyramid standings, and the owner's reflections filed since the previous court, verbatim. The ask is the same for everyone: on_base, off_base and lesson, one to three sentences each, in the seat's own voice, citing actual tickers and numbers — and the lesson must be ONE durable first-person heuristic ("I …") to apply in future sessions, not a recap of today.

    In mock mode the entries are deterministic but data-true, built from the seat's best- and worst-aligned calls (grade minus 50, times the realized return). If an LLM call fails the seat falls back to that same form, so all fifteen entries are always filed. Two lessons from the 2026-08-21 court, as filed:

    The Croupier: "One bet in two coats, and the board's own exit rule already concedes it: NEM's +8.99% is GLD's +4.58% at 1.963x miner beta."

    The Executive: "One book-level correlation is an average of two different graders and tonight it hid the worse one: +0.5175 on twenty leads is a +9.47-point tail spread bolted onto an interior of -0.2304, so from Monday every court I chair reports three numbers instead of one."

    Best call, worst call#

    The Evening view computes two callouts from the scored rows — the lead with the highest and the lowest direction-adjusted day return, with briefing → close. The live court's own report goes further and names the seat whose judgement was best and worst on the day, with the reasoning. On 2026-08-21 the best call was the Croupier's — he "moved NEM from 47 to 72 in a single morning … and made it on a MECHANISM rather than on the last hand" — and the worst the Glazier's: "ROST at 75 was the highest single number written anywhere on this board this morning … and it finished 19th of 20 at -3.03%."

    The Pyramid re-forms#

    After the scoreboard is scored, pyramid.update_pyramid ranks the whole room — the thirteen graders and the Skeptic; the Executive chairs and is not ranked. Per lead with a realized day return, a member's lead score is stance sign × conviction × underlying move: bull +1, bear −1, neutral 0; conviction is |grade − 50| / 50; the underlying move is the day return un-flipped by lead direction. Strongly right earns, strongly wrong bleeds, timid or neutral earns almost nothing. The member's daily score is the mean over its scored leads, stored per (member, run) in pyramid_scores; the standing is an EWMA of daily scores with span 10 sessions, cut into tiers (rank 1 → tier 1; 2–3 → 2; 4–6 → 3; 7–10 → 4; 11 and below → 5). Rank 1 is "in charge of the world today": the next morning every prompt carries its rank one-liner, the Executive is told to weight the leader's grades noticeably more, and the dashboard's leader strip quotes the leader's latest lesson. The Boardroom page draws the standings as a CSS pyramid with a crown on tier 1.

    Journals and dossiers#

    Each entry is one member_journal row — member, run, date, on base, off base, lesson. On the Boardroom page every member card carries a JOURNAL strip (latest lesson and entry count; click to expand recent entries); the member page shows the full journal timeline beside the track record; GET /api/journal returns the newest ten per member. The next morning each seat's five most recent lessons are injected into its grading prompt under "YOUR TRADING JOURNAL — lessons from your recent sessions (apply them)", and into its Pre-Open and Midday prompts too — that is the loop. After the entries are filed the court regenerates the dossiers: one markdown file per seat under data/members/<key>.md with the journal, the grading history with realized outcomes, the Pyramid standing and calibration (also served as /api/member/{key}/dossier and .md). See Learning loops for what is and is not learned.

    The owner's reflections#

    The Pyramid holds the court accountable; reflections hold you accountable. A lead you marked TAKEN owes a reflection once its 1-day outcome lands — the dashboard banner says "✍️ N trade reflection(s) due — the court reads them tonight" — and the form asks what happened (always) and what you would do differently (required when the realized return was negative). Reflections written since the previous court are handed to the Executive's prompt under "THE OWNER'S OWN TRADE REFLECTIONS", verbatim, with the ticker, direction, 1d return and a favorable / unfavorable flag, and the chair is told to weave them into the day's lesson-taking. See Positions & trades.

    The models and training appendix#

    Since round 22 the court also trains. After the journals are on the record and the dossiers refreshed, it calls pulse.evolve.generation() for its own session date — the nightly generation of the five-member actor-critic population the Pulse consults — and carries the record home on a generation block. The step is gated by the rl_evolve_enabled setting (default on), every failure is caught, and a court that did not train says "training did not run: reason" rather than omitting the section; the block is written to data/boardroom/<date>/generation.json and a line is appended to data/rl/self-court.jsonl. The journals are the critical path; nothing in the training half can cost the court its work. From 2026-08-21's block: "NO CHANGE — child m6 (64x37x64 tanh, bred from m2) scored -0.37152 vs m5's -0.36626 on the held-out split; the population is unchanged and every member was still trained and re-scored."

    court_appendix.performance_appendix(run_id) then builds four read-only blocks for the court document, every number copied from the same database readers the Archive uses — never re-averaged or re-rounded:

    run_history
    The last ten completed runs — date, leads, average 1d return, average 5d return, winners — the Archive's own table.
    last_seven_days
    The last seven trading sessions: the book's realized 1d average and winners on each, plus SPY and QQQ close and 1d from the court's recorded close (falling back to that morning's context, and saying which). Sessions with no run say so.
    five_day
    The 5-day column with the count of leads whose window has closed; an open window is named — "5d window still OPEN — 2 of 5 sessions elapsed … closes on …" — never blanked, because a return that does not exist yet must not read as zero. The trading calendar comes from the cached SPY dailies, dates only.
    models
    Generation number, each member's architecture, fitness before and after tonight's training, who was bred, who died, whether the child was admitted, and the deployed-checkpoint line; when evolution did not run, one sentence says why.

    Where it shows#

    The dashboard's MORNING BRIEFING | EVENING COURT toggle switches the view and the theme: evening renders night mode. The Evening view shows the close-of-day index strip and regime, the best / worst callouts, the Scoreboard (rank, ticker, direction, briefing → close, day %, contract last) and The Court Speaks — one card per member with its ON BASE / OFF BASE / LESSON entry, linking to the dossier. Before the first review it reads "The court has not yet convened" with the run button. The Archive replays any past court; the Boardroom page carries the run button and the Pyramid.

    The PDF#

    The in-app Download PDF on the Evening view returns bablytics-evening-court-<date>.pdf — ink and green print design: market at the close, the scoreboard, and the court's per-member ON BASE / OFF BASE / LESSON sections, encrypted with the password you give (AES-256 with the cryptography package, RC4 otherwise). On live-board days the fuller court document built in the day folder (build_evening.py) adds the appendix: a MODELS AND TRAINING section (the generation line, a member table with fitness before and after, the deployed-checkpoint line) and PERFORMANCE — the run-history table, the seven-session strip, the five-day column with open windows named — then the note to the owner and tomorrow's watch.

    API#

    GET /api/review/latest
    {"review": {run_id, review_date, market_close, day_report} | null, "journal_for_run": {member: {on_base, off_base, lesson}}, "members": [...]}
    POST /api/review/trigger · GET /api/review/progress
    Start a forced court in a background thread; the progress payload also carries last_generation, the one-line verdict on the night's training.
    GET /api/journal · GET /api/pyramid
    Journals newest-first (≤10 per member); the standings with score date, tiers and leader.
    GET /api/member/{key}/dossier · /dossier.md
    The dossier as JSON, or the markdown file as a download.
    POST /api/reports/evening/{run_id}
    Body {"password": "…"} → the encrypted court PDF.
    Settings
    review_hour / review_minute (defaults 19:00 ET) via GET/POST /api/settings; rl_evolve_enabled (default "1") gates the night's generation.
